text: The lake lay dark and glossy as the night.
Sunny wandered down the reedy shore.
And gliding on the water, black as velvet,
a graceful swan with beak of ruby red.
She sailed across the stars upon the water,
and left a trail of moonlight in her wake.
“Hello,” said Sunny. “You sail so soft and slow.”
“The night's too beautiful to hurry through.”
The swan curved down her long and elegant neck,
and preened her velvet feathers one by one.
“Each night I tuck the lake in,” said the swan.
“I smooth the water flat as any blanket.”
She glided one last circle, slow and wide,
and everywhere she passed, the ripples slept.
The lake grew still and perfect as a mirror,
with all the stars asleep upon its face.
The swan drifted in among the reeds,
and folded up her wings like evening's curtains.
She tucked her head beneath a velvet wing,
a shadow resting soft upon the water.
Sunny made her bed among the reeds,
where lake songs lapped as gentle as a lullaby.
The shore was still. The water barely breathed.
Everything was peaceful, deep, and safe.
Her eyes grew heavy by the mirrored stars.
One slow blink… then another… then no more.
And Sunny slept beside the velvet swan,
afloat on dreams as smooth as moonlit water.
Goodnight, Sunny. Goodnight, graceful swan.
Goodnight, sleepy lake. Goodnight, little one.
